small_guidance:
- Add channels-last input layout (NHWC) so the GEMM-K dimension (IC*KH*KW) is contiguous along IC — current NCHW layout makes the K-axis strided by H*W, hurting load coalescing. Sweep configs with BLOCK_K=IC (=8) or pad K_TOTAL to 32 since IC*KH*KW=72 is small.
- Since K_TOTAL=72 is tiny, try fully unrolling the K loop (single BLOCK_K=72 or 96 padded) and drop num_stages to 2; also add larger BLOCK_SP (256, 512) configs with BLOCK_OC=32/64 to amortize weight loads across more output pixels.
- Swap grid order to (pid_n, pid_oc, pid_sp) or fuse N and SP into one axis to improve L2 reuse of the weight tile across batches — weights are reused N=128 times and currently each (oc,sp) tile reloads them per batch.
large_guidance:
- Rewrite with NHWC (channels-last) layout end-to-end: permute input once, store output as NHWC then permute back. The im2col gather then reads IC contiguously, enabling vectorized 128-bit loads along K, which is the main bandwidth bottleneck here.
- Use a persistent-CTA design that tiles over (N*OH*OW) output pixels along BLOCK_SP and keeps a full OC tile resident, with KH*KW handled by explicit unrolled 3x3 loops (KH=KW=3 are constexpr). Treat the inner GEMM as a 9-step accumulation of [BLOCK_OC, IC] x [IC, BLOCK_SP] tiles rather than one [BLOCK_OC, 72] x [72, BLOCK_SP] dot — this maps better to small IC=8.
- Fuse a bias-broadcast load outside the K loop (already done) but also consider splitting output along OC into a single program per OC tile that streams over all spatial pixels (persistent), reducing weight reloads from N*ceil(OH*OW/BLOCK_SP) to 1 per CTA.
